chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abdillah ibn Muskhan, from Muhammad al-Halabi, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'If a man divorces his wife while she is in her menstruation period,' he said: 'The divorce is invalid if it is not according to the Sunnah.' I said: 'Then if a man divorces [her] three times in one sitting,' he said: 'It is returned to be considered as one [valid] divorce according to the Sunnah.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man divorces his wife three times while she is menstruating?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq clarifies that a divorce pronounced during menstruation is invalid because it deviates from the Prophetic Sunnah of *Tawqif* (waiting for purity). Specifically, when a man pronounces three divorces in one sitting during this period, they are treated as a single revocable divorce (*raj'i*) rather than three distinct divorces, a ruling that underscores the Shia emphasis on procedural correctness in marital dissolution. This aligns with the broader juristic principle that the timing and manner of the pronouncement are integral to its validity.
